title: overnight inference sprint scratch
content:
Quick overnight sprint scratch (brain dump)
Owner: Aditya Rao — short, noisy, personal.
Context: follow-up after the 03/10 p99 spike that hit a subset of customer routes (mostly 16k+ token requests). Goal: capture triage breadcrumbs, immediate mitigation ideas, and small experiments to run in the morning. Keep short actionable TODOs.

Top goals for next run:
- reproduce p99 spike locally (with smaller scale: 2 replicas, same model variant)
- isolate whether the spike aligns with cache misses vs. batch-size change
- test quick fix: KV-cache retention bump + jittered eviction
- measure impact of switching to quantized-variant (q4f16) for long-seq workloads

Observations from production traces (nightly slice):
- Spike onset: 02:14–02:42 UTC; 87% of affected requests had seq_len >= 12k tokens.
- Correlation: cache_miss rate rose from 6% -> 42% for that route window.
- Throughput: single GPU saw sustained 280 tok/s -> 130 tok/s at spike peak.
- Error rate: not increased (no OOM), just latency tailing.

Immediate hypotheses:
1) Prefix/KV cache thrash: long sequences cause KV footprint to exceed per-replica working set; eviction policy too eager under small memory pressure.
2) Batch-splitting behavior: when sequence lengths above threshold, runtime splits requests incorrectly causing serialization on a single thread.
3) Kernel codepath fallback: for >8192 sequences we fallback to slower attention kernel (small chance).

Quick repro plan (local):
- Dataset: use production-sampled request blob (s3://redwood-prod-samples/longseq/2026-03-10-02.json) — ask infra for a read copy if needed.
- Start a two-replica local cluster:
  ./dev/run_cluster.sh --replicas=2 --model=redwood-open-1 --seq-max=16384 --mem=48G
- Run the loader with 20 concurrent clients, max inflight=8, token rate 1.2x production:
  python tools/loadtest.py --trace sample_longseq.json --concurrency 20 --inflight 8
- Collect: /metrics/rt-p99, /serving/kv-cache/hits, /profiling/llm-kernel/* (flamegraphs)

Quick experiments to try (prioritized):
A. KV-cache: bump retention window from 30s -> 120s and add 25% jitter on eviction timers. Rationale: give time for repeated long requests to reuse prefix cache. Safe to roll back.
B. Batching: cap batch token count to 64k tokens when mean_seq_len > 6k (avoid huge merges).
C. Kernel: force use of broadcast-attn optimized kernel (env override) for a small rollout to 10% traffic.
D. Quantization swap: try q4f16 variant in dedicated staging with same load; measure p95/p99 and quality delta on eval set.

Commands to run (notes to self):
- Toggle cache retention (dev flag):
  curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/_admin/flags -d '{"kv_cache_retention_s":120}'
- Start profiler for 60s:
  curl http://localhost:8080/_debug/profile?dur=60 > run-20260311.pb
  then: ./scripts/convert_pb_to_svg run-20260311.pb > profile.svg
- Disable kernel fallback (local only):
  export RUNTIME_FORCE_OPT_KERNEL=1 && ./bin/serve-local --replicas=2

TODO (owners & ETA):
- [ ] reproduce locally and capture profile (owner: Aditya) — ETA: today morning (3h)
- [ ] run KV-retention bump in staging on small traffic (owner: Mina) — ETA: EOD
- [ ] open small PR for batch token cap heuristic (owner: Sofia) — ETA: tomorrow morning
- [ ] measure quality delta for q4f16 on long-seq eval (owner: Aditya) — ETA: 48h

Notes to mention in Slack (#eng-serving-runtime):
- summary + ask for prod-sample access to reduce friction (link to INF-1203).
- propose temporary canary: 10% traffic -> kv_retention=120s -> monitor p99 for 30m.

Risks & rollback plan:
- KV retention bump can increase memory pressure on small-GPU pools. Rollback: revert flag and auto-scale up GPU count for canary if memory crosses 75%.
- Batch cap may increase per-request latency for some short requests (unlikely); monitor p95 and per-route latency, rollout only if stable for 15m.

Open questions (to discuss at 10:30 sync):
- Do we have telemetry per-GPU memory usage per-replica? (cc: SRE)
- Is there a recent change in kernel selector heuristics? (cc: Rajiv)
- Should we consider per-route cache sizing instead of global retention? Pros/cons quick list.

Brainstorm low-cost mitigations if repro/regression not reproducible:
- route-level throttling for requests with seq_len > 12k (soft 429 with Retry-After)
- on-the-fly fallbacks to a cheaper model variant when tailing is detected
- prefetching strategy: prewarm cache for common prefixes seen in that route (cheap ops)

Final quick log (timeboxed):
- 03:05 — quick check on traces, confirmed cache miss bump
- 03:20 — raised INF-1203 and linked prod traces, pinged Mina for staging run
- 03:40 — sketched test harness and commands (above)

Random notes-to-self (noise):
- keep PRs < 5 files if possible; easier for quick rollback.
- file metrics snapshots to /tmp/metrics-snap-<ts>.json and s3 later.

End scratch. Will convert to a short runbook if the canary looks promising.
